look_here_first: Look at the calendar and the twig before the leaf: cedar elm is a fall-flowering elm with very small rough leaves; corky twig wings, when present, can continue around the leaf node.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: deciduous Texas elm; often common on limestone and clay

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: leaves small, generally under about 5 cm, often obovate/elliptic and bluntish

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: upper leaf surface dark and distinctly rough/scabrous

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: young twigs may develop thin corky wings continuous around nodes

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: flowers in late summer to fall rather than spring

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: small oval samara hairy over the body/edge and deeply notched at apex

key_traits.label: Elm training
key_traits.text: Read leaf texture/asymmetry together with twig wings, bark, reproductive season and samara characters.
